info.title: FHIR Server
info.description: FHIR R4-compliant REST API server for managing healthcare resources. Supports 34 FHIR R4 resources with dual-format responses (application/json and application/fhir+json). Pure CRUD data layer — no auth, no business rules. Designed for integration with AI agents via FastMCP dynamic tool generation.

get.description: Returns 200 if the process is running. Use for liveness probes — does not check DB or Redis. No authentication required.
Returns 200 only when the database and Redis are reachable. Use for readiness probes — orchestrators should stop routing traffic to this instance when it returns 503. No authentication required.

503.description: One or more dependencies are unavailable

post.summary: Create an organization FHIR profile (as a draft)
post.description: Creates a scope_level='organization' profile row, always as status='draft'. Country and base profiles have no write path here — see CreatableProfileScopeLevel's own docstring (app/schemas/fhir_profile.py) for why country was locked out of this endpoint too. The parent is resolved automatically: this resource_type's active country profile for this deployment's configured country if one exists, else base. The candidate structure_definition is run past the Java validator sidecar's registration check before being persisted; a rejection returns 422 with the sidecar's own errors. Use the activate endpoint to make a draft take effect — this endpoint never does.

scope_level.description:
Which layer of the base -> country -> organization profile chain a
row represents — see docs/structure-definitions/12-three-layer-validation-architecture.md.
Permanently fixed by this project's own design, not a FHIR terminology
binding — a real Postgres Enum is the right call here the same way
CLAUDE.md's "Category A" (required-binding, spec-fixed value sets)
applies to FHIR's own enums. Member names are lowercase, matching their
values exactly — this project's own established convention (see
IdentifierUse in app/models/enums.py) for keeping the Postgres enum's
stored labels equal to the Python value, not the member name.
scope_level.title: FhirProfileScopeLevel

status.description:
This app's own "is this the profile layer currently enforced for
its scope" flag — NOT a mirror of the StructureDefinition's own
"status" field inside `structure_definition` (that's a different,
HL7-defined concept: the resource's publication maturity, which can
legitimately say "draft" for a profile that's fully live here, e.g.
HL7's own real R4 Organization entry, or country_in.json before this
was wired up). Reuses the same four FHIR status names only because
they're a convenient, already-defined vocabulary for "not live yet /
live / superseded / unknown", not because this column tracks what
those names mean in the spec.

Base rows: no draft -> active -> retired lifecycle at all — exactly
one row per resource_type, seeded directly as 'active' (see
seed_base_profiles.py), never created or activated through
FhirProfileService.

Country/organization rows: a real lifecycle —
FhirProfileService.create_profile() always inserts 'draft';
activate_profile() is the only path to 'active', and atomically
retires whatever was active before it for the same scope. Seeded
country rows (seed_country_profiles.py) are the one exception — they
go in directly as 'active', since seeding is this app's own ground
truth, not a draft awaiting admin action.
status.title: FhirProfileStatus

post.summary: Activate a draft profile, retiring whatever was active for the same scope
post.description: Atomically retires the previously-active row (if any) for this profile's own (resource_type, scope_level, scope_id) and activates this one, then evicts the matching fhir_profile_cache entry. A retired profile cannot be reactivated directly — create a new version instead.

post.summary: Create a new Location resource
post.description: Records details and position information for a physical place where services are provided and resources and participants may be stored, found, contained, or accommodated. The request body is a FHIR R4 Location resource (camelCase, nested datatypes — https://www.hl7.org/fhir/R4/location.html), stored atomically in one DB transaction. The body is checked against base FHIR R4: any valid R4 element is accepted and stored as sent (server-managed `id`/`meta` are ignored); a key that isn't FHIR at all is rejected with 422. `managingOrganization` (`Organization/<id>`), `partOf` (`Location/<id>`) and `identifier.assigner` relative references must exist in the caller's org (422 otherwise); absolute URLs are stored without a check. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

anyOf.description:
FHIR R4 Meta — infrastructure-maintained metadata about a resource.
`lastUpdated` is the only field this server populates natively today
(from the row's `updated_at`); `security`/`tag` reuse FHIRCoding since
both are 0..* Coding per spec. `extension` is where resource metadata
with no native Meta field rides — e.g. Organization's `org_id`/
`created_by`/`updated_by`/`created_at` (see
app.fhir.mappers.organization.fhir._fhir_meta) — same raw,
not-yet-registered-extension-definition convention as a resource's own
top-level `extension` field.

get.description: FHIR R4 search (https://www.hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html) over Location. Search parameters: `_id`, `_lastUpdated`, `address`, `address-city`, `address-country`, `address-postalcode`, `address-state`, `address-use`, `endpoint`, `identifier`, `name`, `near`, `operational-status`, `organization`, `partof`, `status`, `type` — each with the modifiers listed on it. A comma-separated value list ORs; repeating a parameter ANDs. A known parameter with an unsupported modifier or a malformed value is rejected with 400 (OperationOutcome). Unknown parameters are ignored and reported in an `outcome` entry, or rejected with `Prefer: handling=strict`. Not supported (ignored as unknown): `_tag`, `_profile`, `_security`, `_source`, `_text`, `_content`, `_list`, `_has`, `_type`, `_filter`; `_query` is always rejected. Returns a searchset Bundle with `total`, `link` (self/first/previous/next/last) and entries carrying `fullUrl` and `search.mode`. Always scoped to the caller's own org (from the verified token) — `org_id` is not a client-suppliable filter. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

parameters.name: _id
parameters.description: Logical id of the resource (the public location id) (R4 expression: `Resource.id`). FHIR `token` search: `code`, `system|code`, `|code` (no system) or `system|` (any code in system). Codes match exactly. Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all). `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

parameters.name: _id:not
parameters.description: _id with `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all).

parameters.name: _id:missing
parameters.description: _id with `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

406.description: Not Acceptable — the Accept header or `_format` rules out JSON (e.g. XML only); FHIR JSON is the only format served. Body is an OperationOutcome.

patch.description: The request body is a partial FHIR R4 Location (merge-patch on top-level elements). Only supplied elements are written; omitted elements are left unchanged. A supplied list (identifier, type, alias, telecom, hoursOfOperation, endpoint — even `[]`) replaces the stored entries; a supplied object (`address`, `position`, `managingOrganization`, `partOf`, ...) replaces the whole element, and `null` clears it. Rejected with 422 if a referenced Organization/Location doesn't exist, or if `partOf` would create a circular hierarchy. Scoped to the caller's own org — patch_location() raises NotFoundError (404, not 403 — avoids leaking that a location with this id exists in another org) if actor.org_id doesn't match. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

not-yet-registered-extension-definition convention as a resource's own
top-level `extension` field.

422.description: Validation error — request body failed schema validation

delete.description: Permanently deletes the Location (and its search-index rows). Scoped to the caller's own org — raises NotFoundError (404, not 403) if the location exists but belongs to a different org. Returns 204 on success.

parameters.name: location_id
parameters.description: Public location identifier.

406.description: Not Acceptable — the Accept header or `_format` rules out JSON (e.g. XML only); FHIR JSON is the only format served. Body is an OperationOutcome.

post.summary: Search Location resources (FHIR R4 search via POST)
post.description: Same search as `GET /`, with the parameters sent as an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body (R4 `POST [base]/[type]/_search`) — use it when the query string would be too long, or to keep search values out of URLs. Query-string parameters, if any, are combined with the body. FHIR R4 search (https://www.hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html) over Location. Search parameters: `_id`, `_lastUpdated`, `address`, `address-city`, `address-country`, `address-postalcode`, `address-state`, `address-use`, `endpoint`, `identifier`, `name`, `near`, `operational-status`, `organization`, `partof`, `status`, `type` — each with the modifiers listed on it. A comma-separated value list ORs; repeating a parameter ANDs. A known parameter with an unsupported modifier or a malformed value is rejected with 400 (OperationOutcome). Unknown parameters are ignored and reported in an `outcome` entry, or rejected with `Prefer: handling=strict`. Not supported (ignored as unknown): `_tag`, `_profile`, `_security`, `_source`, `_text`, `_content`, `_list`, `_has`, `_type`, `_filter`; `_query` is always rejected. Returns a searchset Bundle with `total`, `link` (self/first/previous/next/last) and entries carrying `fullUrl` and `search.mode`. Always scoped to the caller's own org (from the verified token) — `org_id` is not a client-suppliable filter. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

200.description: FHIR searchset Bundle: matches (search.mode=match), _include/_revinclude results (include) and any ignored-parameter warning (outcome)

type.description: The purpose of this bundle. Always 'searchset' in this API.
type.title: Type

total.description: Number of matches across all pages (not counting included resources). Omitted with _total=none.
total.title: Total

fullUrl.description: Absolute URL of the resource (absent on an outcome entry).
fullUrl.title: Fullurl

anyOf.description:
FHIR R4 Meta — infrastructure-maintained metadata about a resource.
`lastUpdated` is the only field this server populates natively today
(from the row's `updated_at`); `security`/`tag` reuse FHIRCoding since
both are 0..* Coding per spec. `extension` is where resource metadata
with no native Meta field rides — e.g. Organization's `org_id`/
`created_by`/`updated_by`/`created_at` (see
app.fhir.mappers.organization.fhir._fhir_meta) — same raw,
not-yet-registered-extension-definition convention as a resource's own
top-level `extension` field.

post.summary: Create a new Organization resource
post.description: Records a formally or informally recognized grouping of people or organizations formed for the purpose of achieving some form of collective action. The request body is a FHIR R4 Organization resource (camelCase, nested datatypes — https://www.hl7.org/fhir/R4/organization.html); the organization and every supplied element (identifier, type, alias, telecom, address, contact, endpoint) are written atomically in one DB transaction. The body is checked against base FHIR R4: any valid R4 element is accepted and stored as sent (server-managed `id`/`meta` are ignored); a key that isn't FHIR at all is rejected with 422. Optionally link to a parent organization via `partOf` (e.g. `{"reference": "Organization/190001"}`) — rejected with 422 if the referenced organization doesn't exist. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

406.description: Not Acceptable — the Accept header or `_format` rules out JSON (e.g. XML only); FHIR JSON is the only format served. Body is an OperationOutcome.

422.description: Validation error — request body failed schema validation

get.description: FHIR R4 search (https://www.hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html) over Organization. Search parameters: `_id`, `_lastUpdated`, `active`, `address`, `address-city`, `address-country`, `address-postalcode`, `address-state`, `address-use`, `endpoint`, `identifier`, `name`, `partof`, `phonetic`, `type` — each with the modifiers listed on it. A comma-separated value list ORs; repeating a parameter ANDs. A known parameter with an unsupported modifier or a malformed value is rejected with 400 (OperationOutcome). Unknown parameters are ignored and reported in an `outcome` entry, or rejected with `Prefer: handling=strict`. Not supported (ignored as unknown): `_tag`, `_profile`, `_security`, `_source`, `_text`, `_content`, `_list`, `_has`, `_type`, `_filter`; `_query` is always rejected. Returns a searchset Bundle with `total`, `link` (self/first/previous/next/last) and entries carrying `fullUrl` and `search.mode`. Always scoped to the caller's own org (from the verified token) — `org_id` is not a client-suppliable filter. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

200.description: FHIR searchset Bundle: matches (search.mode=match), _include/_revinclude results (include) and any ignored-parameter warning (outcome)

type.description: The purpose of this bundle. Always 'searchset' in this API.
type.title: Type

total.description: Number of matches across all pages (not counting included resources). Omitted with _total=none.
total.title: Total

fullUrl.description: Absolute URL of the resource (absent on an outcome entry).
fullUrl.title: Fullurl

406.description: Not Acceptable — the Accept header or `_format` rules out JSON (e.g. XML only); FHIR JSON is the only format served. Body is an OperationOutcome.

patch.description: The request body is a partial FHIR R4 Organization (merge-patch on top-level elements). Only supplied elements are written; omitted elements are left unchanged. Every supplied list (identifier, type, alias, telecom, address, contact, endpoint — even `[]`) atomically replaces the stored entries; a supplied `partOf` replaces the whole Reference, and `null` clears it — rejected with 422 if the referenced organization doesn't exist or setting it would create a circular hierarchy. Scoped to the caller's own org — patch_organization() raises NotFoundError (404, not 403 — avoids leaking that an organization with this id exists in another org) if actor.org_id doesn't match. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

`lastUpdated` is the only field this server populates natively today
(from the row's `updated_at`); `security`/`tag` reuse FHIRCoding since
both are 0..* Coding per spec. `extension` is where resource metadata
with no native Meta field rides — e.g. Organization's `org_id`/
`created_by`/`updated_by`/`created_at` (see
app.fhir.mappers.organization.fhir._fhir_meta) — same raw,
not-yet-registered-extension-definition convention as a resource's own
top-level `extension` field.

post.summary: Search Organization resources (FHIR R4 search via POST)
post.description: Same search as `GET /`, with the parameters sent as an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body (R4 `POST [base]/[type]/_search`) — use it when the query string would be too long, or to keep search values out of URLs. Query-string parameters, if any, are combined with the body. FHIR R4 search (https://www.hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html) over Organization. Search parameters: `_id`, `_lastUpdated`, `active`, `address`, `address-city`, `address-country`, `address-postalcode`, `address-state`, `address-use`, `endpoint`, `identifier`, `name`, `partof`, `phonetic`, `type` — each with the modifiers listed on it. A comma-separated value list ORs; repeating a parameter ANDs. A known parameter with an unsupported modifier or a malformed value is rejected with 400 (OperationOutcome). Unknown parameters are ignored and reported in an `outcome` entry, or rejected with `Prefer: handling=strict`. Not supported (ignored as unknown): `_tag`, `_profile`, `_security`, `_source`, `_text`, `_content`, `_list`, `_has`, `_type`, `_filter`; `_query` is always rejected. Returns a searchset Bundle with `total`, `link` (self/first/previous/next/last) and entries carrying `fullUrl` and `search.mode`. Always scoped to the caller's own org (from the verified token) — `org_id` is not a client-suppliable filter. Always responds with FHIR R4 JSON (`application/fhir+json`), whatever the Accept header says; only a client that accepts no JSON at all (e.g. `Accept: application/fhir+xml`, `_format=xml`) gets 406 Not Acceptable.

Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:contains` — the value appears anywhere in the field (case/accent-insensitive). `:exact` — the whole field equals the value, case- and accent-sensitive. `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

address-postalcode:contains.description: address-postalcode with `:contains` — the value appears anywhere in the field (case/accent-insensitive).

address-postalcode:exact.description: address-postalcode with `:exact` — the whole field equals the value, case- and accent-sensitive.

address-postalcode:missing.description: address-postalcode with `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

address-state.description: A state specified in an address (R4 expression: `Organization.address.state`). FHIR `string` search: matches when the field equals or STARTS WITH the value, ignoring case and accents (`name=gen` matches 'General Hospital', `name=hopital` matches 'Hôpital'). Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:contains` — the value appears anywhere in the field (case/accent-insensitive). `:exact` — the whole field equals the value, case- and accent-sensitive. `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

address-state:contains.description: address-state with `:contains` — the value appears anywhere in the field (case/accent-insensitive).

address-state:exact.description: address-state with `:exact` — the whole field equals the value, case- and accent-sensitive.

address-state:missing.description: address-state with `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

address-use.description: A use code specified in an address (home | work | temp | old | billing; system http://hl7.org/fhir/address-use) (R4 expression: `Organization.address.use`). FHIR `token` search: `code`, `system|code`, `|code` (no system) or `system|` (any code in system). Codes match exactly. Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all). `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

address-use:not.description: address-use with `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all).

address-use:missing.description: address-use with `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

endpoint.description: Technical endpoints providing access to services operated for the organization (R4 expression: `Organization.endpoint`). FHIR `reference` search: `[id]`, `[type]/[id]` or an absolute URL (an absolute URL on this server matches its relative form). Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:identifier` — matches Reference.identifier as a token: `[system|]value`. `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one. `:Endpoint` — restrict to that target type (value is the bare id).

endpoint:identifier.description: endpoint with `:identifier` — matches Reference.identifier as a token: `[system|]value`.

endpoint:missing.description: endpoint with `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

endpoint:Endpoint.description: endpoint restricted to Endpoint references; value is the Endpoint id.

identifier.description: Any identifier for the organization (not the accreditation issuer's identifier) (R4 expression: `Organization.identifier`). FHIR `token` search: `code`, `system|code`, `|code` (no system) or `system|` (any code in system). Codes match exactly. Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all). `:of-type` — identifier of a given type: `type-system|type-code|value` (all three required). `:text` — string search (starts-with) on Identifier.type.text / type.coding.display. `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

identifier:not.description: identifier with `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all).

identifier:of-type.description: identifier with `:of-type` — identifier of a given type: `type-system|type-code|value` (all three required).

identifier:missing.description: identifier with `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

name.description: A portion of the organization's name or alias (R4 expression: `Organization.name | Organization.alias`). FHIR `string` search: matches when the field equals or STARTS WITH the value, ignoring case and accents (`name=gen` matches 'General Hospital', `name=hopital` matches 'Hôpital'). Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:contains` — the value appears anywhere in the field (case/accent-insensitive). `:exact` — the whole field equals the value, case- and accent-sensitive. `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

partof.description: An organization of which this organization forms a part (R4 expression: `Organization.partOf`). FHIR `reference` search: `[id]`, `[type]/[id]` or an absolute URL (an absolute URL on this server matches its relative form). Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:above` — organizations whose partOf is the given one or any of its ancestors. `:below` — organizations anywhere below the given one in the partOf hierarchy (children, grandchildren, ...). `:identifier` — matches Reference.identifier as a token: `[system|]value`. `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one. `:Organization` — restrict to that target type (value is the bare id). Chaining: `partof.<param>=value` applies any Organization search parameter (with its modifiers) to the referenced resource, e.g. `partof.name=Acme`, `partof.partof.name=Acme`.

phonetic.description: A portion of the organization's name using some kind of phonetic matching algorithm (American Soundex, word by word; the first letter must match) (R4 expression: `Organization.name`). FHIR `string` search: matches when the field equals or STARTS WITH the value, ignoring case and accents (`name=gen` matches 'General Hospital', `name=hopital` matches 'Hôpital'). Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

type.description: A code for the type of organization (R4 expression: `Organization.type`). FHIR `token` search: `code`, `system|code`, `|code` (no system) or `system|` (any code in system). Codes match exactly. Comma-separated values are OR'd (`a,b`); repeating the parameter ANDs. Escape a literal `,` `|` `$` or `\` with a backslash. Modifiers: `:above` — the code, or any code that subsumes it (IS-A ancestors in the terminology service): `[system|]code`. `:below` — the code, or any code it subsumes (IS-A descendants in the terminology service): `[system|]code`. `:in` — the code is in the given ValueSet (canonical URL, `url|version` or `ValueSet/<id>`), per the terminology service. `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all). `:not-in` — no code is in the given ValueSet. `:text` — string search (starts-with, case/accent-insensitive) on the code's text/display instead of the code. `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

type:above.description: type with `:above` — the code, or any code that subsumes it (IS-A ancestors in the terminology service): `[system|]code`.

type:below.description: type with `:below` — the code, or any code it subsumes (IS-A descendants in the terminology service): `[system|]code`.

type:in.description: type with `:in` — the code is in the given ValueSet (canonical URL, `url|version` or `ValueSet/<id>`), per the terminology service.

type:not.description: type with `:not` — resources with no matching code (includes resources with no value at all).

type:not-in.description: type with `:not-in` — no code is in the given ValueSet.

type:text.description: type with `:text` — string search (starts-with, case/accent-insensitive) on the code's text/display instead of the code.

type:missing.description: type with `:missing=true` — resources with no value for this parameter; `:missing=false` — resources that have one.

_count.description: Page size (default 50, max 200; larger values are capped). `_count=0` returns only the total.

_offset.description: Number of matches to skip (paging; the Bundle's next/previous links carry it).

_sort.description: Comma-separated sort parameters, `-` prefix for descending. Sortable: _id, _lastUpdated, active, address-city, address-country, address-postalcode, address-state, identifier, name, partof, phonetic, type. Default: newest first (`-_id`).

_total.description: `accurate` (default) counts every match; `none` skips the count (Bundle.total omitted); `estimate` = accurate.

_summary.description: `true` — summary elements only (active, identifier, name, partOf, type); `text` — id, meta, narrative; `data` — everything but the narrative; `count` — total only, no entries; `false` (default) — the full resource. Subsetted resources carry the SUBSETTED meta tag.

_elements.description: Comma-separated top-level elements to return (id and meta are always included), e.g. `name,identifier`.

_include.description: Also return resources the matches reference: Organization:partof, Organization:endpoint, or `*`. `_include:iterate` repeats it on included resources.

_include:iterate.description: Iterative _include: Organization:partof, Organization:endpoint applied again to each included resource.

_revinclude.description: Also return resources that reference the matches: Organization:partof, Location:organization, or `*`. `_revinclude:iterate` repeats it.

_revinclude:iterate.description: Iterative _revinclude: Organization:partof, Location:organization applied again to each included resource.

_format.description: Only JSON is supported; anything else (e.g. `xml`) is 406 Not Acceptable.

post.description: Accepts any FHIR R4 resource JSON body (resourceType is read directly from it — this isn't scoped to one resource type) and runs it through the exact same validate_resource() dispatch every resource's own create/patch path uses internally: base, narrowed by a country profile if settings.fhir_validation.country has one active for this resource type, narrowed further by org_id's own active profile if one exists and org_id is passed. Always returns 200 with a FHIR OperationOutcome — this is a diagnostic tool for exploring what a payload would fail on, not a gate, so an invalid resource is a normal, successful response (one OperationOutcome.issue per problem found), not an error. CreatableProfileScopeLevel.title: CreatableProfileScopeLevel
CreatableProfileScopeLevel.description:
The only scope_level value valid for FhirProfileCreateSchema —
deliberately narrower than app.models.fhir_profile.enums.FhirProfileScopeLevel,
which also has 'base' and 'country'.

'base' is seeded once from the HL7 bundle (see scripts/profiling/
seed_base_profiles.py), never created through this endpoint.

'country' is EXCLUDED here too (this endpoint used to allow it) —
a country profile is a deployment-wide, rarely-changing decision with
its own dedicated write path (scripts/profiling/seed_country_profiles.py,
reading scripts/data/profiling/resources/<type>/country_<code>.json
straight into the DB as 'active', bypassing this schema/service
entirely), and app.fhir.validation.dispatch.register_configured_country_profiles()
now eagerly loads + registers every active country profile with the
Java validator sidecar once, at application startup. Exposing live
create/update of a country profile through this HTTP endpoint would
let it drift out of step with that startup-time registration — an
edit here wouldn't be picked up by the sidecar until the next
restart, and this endpoint has no code to re-run the startup preload
on demand. Re-seed via the script above (then restart the process) to
change a country profile instead.

FhirProfileService.create_profile() rejects both 'base' and 'country'
with a 422 at runtime as defense-in-depth for any caller that doesn't
go through this schema — narrowing the type here just means a bad
value (a typo, or either excluded value) gets a clean Pydantic
validation error before the request reaches the service at all.

FhirPeriodInput.description:
FHIR R4 Period. Typed as `datetime` because every Period this project
stores lands in a `DateTime(timezone=True)` column. A timezone-naive
value passes Pydantic but is still rejected by base R4 validation (FHIR's
dateTime requires an offset whenever a time is present).

scope_id.title: Scope Id
scope_id.description: Must be omitted — the org_id is derived from the verified JWT (activeOrganizationId) instead, never from this field.

FhirProfileCreateSchema.title: FhirProfileCreateSchema
FhirProfileCreateSchema.description:
Create an organization profile — never base or country, neither of
which have a write path here (see CreatableProfileScopeLevel's own
docstring for why country was removed from this endpoint too).

`scope_id` must be OMITTED here entirely — the router derives it from
the verified JWT's activeOrganizationId claim (actor.org_id) instead,
same as every org-scoped resource in this codebase (see CLAUDE.md's
Multi-Tenancy & Ownership). A caller can only ever create an
organization-scope profile for their OWN org, never one named in the
request body.

The service resolves this profile's parent itself (the active country
profile for this deployment's configured country if one exists for
this resource_type, else base — re-checked fresh on every write, not
assumed from a prior one) and overwrites whatever
`structure_definition['baseDefinition']` the caller sent to match —
the chain is enforced server-side, not trusted from the request.

`structure_definition['url']` is always auto-derived (from `scope_id`
+ `resource_type`, the same convention app.fhir.validation.dispatch
falls back to) and unconditionally overwritten, never trusted from the
request — a client-supplied value could drift from the real identity
this profile is scoped to, or collide with another org's profile.

`structure_definition['id']` (the base FHIR Resource.id, distinct from
`url` — nothing in this pipeline reads or relies on it) is ALWAYS
server-generated as a fresh UUID4 — a client-supplied value is
silently overwritten, never required.

`created_by` is NOT a field here — same as every other currently-built
resource (see CLAUDE.md's Multi-Tenancy & Ownership), it comes from the
verified JWT's `sub` at the router layer, not the request body.

FhirProfilePatchSchema.title: FhirProfilePatchSchema
FhirProfilePatchSchema.description:
Replaces a draft profile's structure_definition wholesale — only
valid while status='draft'; an active or retired row is immutable
history (create a new version via FhirProfileCreateSchema instead).

`updated_by` is NOT a field here — comes from the verified JWT's `sub`
at the router layer, same as every other currently-built resource.
